title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固
title.en: Volume 88 Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固 Volume 88 Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固

translations.literal: Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, and Cui Daogu

sentences.zh: 薛安都，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Andou was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世為強族，同姓有三千家。

translations.literal: For generations they were a powerful clan; those of the same surname numbered three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a powerful clan for generations, with three thousand households of the same surname.

sentences.zh: 父廣，為宗豪，高祖定關、河，以為上黨太守。

translations.literal: His father Guang was a clan magnate; when the Founding Emperor pacified Guan and the Yellow River region, he was made Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang was a leader of the clan; when the Founding Emperor secured Guan and the Yellow River lands, he appointed him Administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 安都少以勇聞，身長七尺八寸，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Andou was known from youth for courage; his height was seven feet eight inches, and he was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was famed from youth for his bravery. He stood seven feet eight inches tall and was expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 索虜使助秦州刺史北賀汨擊反胡白龍子，滅之。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei sent him to assist the Qinzhou Inspector Bei Hewen in attacking the rebel Hu Bailongzi and destroying him.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei sent him to aid Qinzhou Inspector Bei Hewen in crushing the rebel Hu Bailongzi.

sentences.zh: 由是為偽雍、秦二州都統，州各有刺史，都統總其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made overall commander of the false Yong and Qin provinces; each province had its own inspector, but the commander-in-chief oversaw all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made overall commander of the puppet Yong and Qin provinces, each with its own inspector while he held supreme command.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，索虜主拓跋燾擊芮芮大敗，安都與宗人薛永宗起義，永宗營汾曲，安都襲得弘農。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao suffered a great defeat attacking the Rouran; Andou rose in revolt with his clansman Xue Yongzong—Yongzong encamped at Fenqu, Andou seized Hongnong by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 21, after Tuoba Tao of the Northern Wei suffered a crushing defeat against the Rouran, Andou joined his kinsman Xue Yongzong in revolt. Yongzong camped along the Fen River bend while Andou took Hongnong by surprise.

sentences.zh: 會北地人蓋吳起兵，遂連衡相應。

translations.literal: It happened that Gai Wu of Beidi raised troops, and they formed an alliance and responded to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Wu of Beidi rose in arms, they allied and acted in concert.

sentences.zh: 燾自率眾擊永宗，滅其族，進擊蓋吳。

translations.literal: Tao personally led his troops to attack Yongzong, exterminated his clan, and advanced to attack Gai Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao led his army in person against Yongzong, wiped out his clan, and marched on Gai Wu.

sentences.zh: 安都料眾寡不敵，率壯士辛靈度等，棄弘農歸國。

translations.literal: Andou judged his forces too few to resist; he led stalwarts including Xin Lingdu, abandoned Hongnong, and returned to the [Song] state.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his forces outmatched, Andou led brave men such as Xin Lingdu, gave up Hongnong, and defected to Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖延見之，求北還構扇河、陝，招聚義眾。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor received him in audience; [Andou] asked to go north again to stir up rebellion in the He and Shaanxi regions and gather righteous followers.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor granted him an audience. Andou asked to return north to raise rebellion in the Yellow River and Shaanxi regions and rally loyal forces.

sentences.zh: 上許之，給錦百匹，雜繒三百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor consented and gave him a hundred bolts of brocade and three hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and gave him a hundred bolts of brocade and three hundred bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 復襲弘農，虜已增戍，城不可克，蓋吳又死，乃退還上洛。

translations.literal: He again attacked Hongnong, but the barbarians had strengthened the garrison and the city could not be taken; Gai Wu also died, so he withdrew to Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: He struck at Hongnong again, but the enemy had reinforced the garrison and the city would not fall. Gai Wu had also died, so he fell back to Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮襄陽，板為揚武將軍、北弘農太守。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was stationed at Xiangyang, [Andou] was appointed on his staff as General Who Raises Martiality and Administrator of Northern Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent held Xiangyang, Andou was appointed on his staff as General Who Raises Martiality and Administrator of Northern Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 虜漸強盛，安都乃歸襄陽。

translations.literal: As the barbarians grew stronger, Andou returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the Northern Wei grew stronger, Andou withdrew to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從叔沈亦同歸國，官至綏遠將軍、新野太守。

translations.literal: His cousin Shen also returned to the [Song] state with him and rose to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Shen defected with him and eventually reached the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隨王誕版安都為建武將軍，隨柳元景向關、陝，率步騎居前，所向克捷，事在元景傳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Prince of Suiwang Dan commissioned Andou as General Who Establishes Martiality; with Liu Yuanjing he marched toward Guan and Shaanxi, leading infantry and cavalry at the van and winning wherever he went—the details are in Yuanjing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, Prince Dan of Sui commissioned Andou as General Who Establishes Martiality. With Liu Yuanjing he advanced on Guan and Shaanxi at the head of the infantry and cavalry and carried every fight—the full account is in Yuanjing's biography.

sentences.zh: 軍還，誕版為後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Dan commissioned him as acting staff officer of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign, Dan appointed him acting staff officer of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，除始興王濬征北行參軍，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was made acting staff officer on the northern campaign of Prince of Shixing Jun, with the additional title General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he was made acting staff officer on Prince Jun of Shixing's northern campaign, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Martiality.

sentences.zh: 魯爽向虎牢，安都復隨元景北出，即據關城，期俱濟河取蒲阪。

translations.literal: Lu Shuang advanced on Hulao; Andou again followed Yuanjing north, immediately seized Tong Pass, and planned to cross the river together and take Puban.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shuang marched on Hulao, Andou again went north with Yuanjing, seized Tong Pass at once, and planned to cross the river together and take Puban.

sentences.zh: 會爽退，安都復率所領隨元景引還。

translations.literal: When Shuang withdrew, Andou again led his command and followed Yuanjing back.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang retreated, Andou led his troops back with Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 仍伐西陽五水蠻。

translations.literal: He then campaigned against the Five-Water Man of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned against the Five-Water Man tribes of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐逆，轉參軍事，加寧朔將軍，領馬軍，與柳元景俱發。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent campaigned against the usurper, [Andou] was transferred to staff duty, given the additional rank General Who Pacifies the North, and put in command of the horse army; he set out with Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent marched against the usurper, Andou was transferred to staff duty, promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, and given command of the cavalry. He set out with Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 四月十四日，至朱雀航，橫矛瞋目，叱賊將皇甫安民等曰：「賊弑君父，何心事之！

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month, they reached Zhuque Ford; [Andou] levelled his spear, glared, and shouted at the rebel generals Huangfu Anmin and others: "The rebels murdered their sovereign and father—why do you serve them!
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month they reached Zhuque Ford. Andou levelled his spear, glared, and shouted at the rebel generals Huangfu Anmin and the rest: "These rebels murdered their lord and father—why do you serve them?

sentences.zh: 」世祖踐阼，除右軍將軍。

translations.literal: " When the Heir Apparent ascended the throne, [Andou] was made General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Heir Apparent took the throne, Andou was appointed General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 五月四日，率所領騎為前鋒，直入殿庭。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fifth month, he led his cavalry as vanguard and charged straight into the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fifth month he led his cavalry as vanguard straight into the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 賊尚有數百人，一時奔散。

translations.literal: Several hundred rebels remained; all at once they fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred rebels still held the ground, but they broke and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 以功封南鄉縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 安都從征關、陝，至臼口，夢仰頭視天，正見天門開，謂左右曰：「汝見天門開不？

translations.literal: Andou followed the campaign to Guan and Shaanxi; at Jiukou he dreamed he looked up at heaven and saw the Heavenly Gate open; he said to those beside him: "Do you see the Heavenly Gate open?
translations.idiomatic: On the Guan-Shaanxi campaign, at Jiukou, Andou dreamed he looked up and saw the gates of heaven open. He asked his attendants: "Do you see the gates of heaven open?

sentences.zh: 」至是歎曰：「夢天開，乃中興之象邪！」

translations.literal: " Now he sighed and said: "To dream heaven opens—is that not an omen of restoration!"
translations.idiomatic: " Now he sighed and said: "A dream of heaven opening—surely that is an omen of dynastic renewal!"

sentences.zh: 從弟道生，亦以軍功為大司馬參軍。

translations.literal: His cousin Daosheng also, through military merit, became a staff officer of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Daosheng had likewise won a post as staff officer to the Grand Marshal through military service.

sentences.zh: 犯罪，為秣陵令庾淑之所鞭。

translations.literal: He committed a crime and was flogged by Yu Shuzhi, magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the law and was flogged by Yu Shuzhi, magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 安都大怒，乃乘馬從數十人，令左右執矟，欲往殺淑之。

translations.literal: Andou was furious; he mounted his horse with several dozen men, ordered his attendants to take spears, and intended to go kill Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Andou flew into a rage, mounted his horse with several dozen followers, had his men take spears, and set out to kill Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 行至朱雀航，逢柳元景。

translations.literal: As he reached Zhuque Ford he met Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuque Ford he met Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 元景遙問：「薛公何處去？

translations.literal: Yuanjing called from afar: "Lord Xue, where are you going?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing called from a distance: "Lord Xue, where are you bound?

sentences.zh: 」安都躍馬至車後曰：「小子庾淑之鞭我從弟，今詣往刺殺之。

translations.literal: " Andou spurred his horse to the rear of the carriage and said: "That whelp Yu Shuzhi flogged my cousin—I am going now to stab and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " Andou spurred up to the rear of the carriage and said: "That whelp Yu Shuzhi flogged my cousin. I am on my way to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」元景慮其不可駐，乃紿之曰：「小子無宜適，卿往與手，甚快。

translations.literal: " Yuanjing feared he could not be stopped, so he deceived him, saying: "The whelp deserves it; if you go and strike him yourself, how satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanjing feared he could not be stopped, so he deceived him: "The wretch had it coming. If you go and strike him yourself, all the better.

sentences.zh: 」安都既回馬，復追呼之：「別宜與卿有所論。

translations.literal: " Andou had already turned his horse when [Yuanjing] called after him again: "Wait—I have something else to discuss with you.
translations.idiomatic: " Andou had already wheeled about when Yuanjing called after him: "Wait—I have something else to say to you.

sentences.zh: 」令下馬入車。

translations.literal: " He ordered him to dismount and enter the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He told him to dismount and get into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 既入車，因責讓之曰：「卿從弟服章言論，與寒細不異，雖復人士，庾淑之亦何由得知？

translations.literal: Once he was in the carriage, [Yuanjing] rebuked him, saying: "Your cousin's dress and speech are no different from those of the lowly—even if he were a gentleman, how was Yu Shuzhi to know?
translations.idiomatic: Once Andou was inside, Yuanjing rebuked him: "Your cousin's dress and speech are no better than a commoner's. Even if he were a gentleman, how was Yu Shuzhi to know?

sentences.zh: 且人身犯罪，理應加罰，卿為朝廷勳臣，宜崇奉法憲，云何放恣，輒欲於都邑殺人？

translations.literal: Moreover, when a man commits a crime he ought by right to be punished. You are a meritorious minister of the court and should uphold the laws—why indulge yourself and want to kill a man in the capital?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when a man breaks the law he deserves punishment. You are a meritorious servant of the throne and ought to uphold the statutes. Why give way to rage and try to kill a man in the capital?

sentences.zh: 非唯科律所不容，主上亦無辭以相宥。

translations.literal: This is not only what the statutes will not allow—the sovereign also will have no words with which to pardon you.
translations.idiomatic: The law will not tolerate it, and the emperor will have no grounds to spare you.

sentences.zh: 」因載之俱歸，安都乃止。

translations.literal: " He then took him back together, and Andou stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He took him back in the carriage, and Andou abandoned his plan.

sentences.zh: 其年，以憚直免官。

translations.literal: That year, because of his fearlessness and bluntness, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was removed from office for his blunt fearlessness.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，復除左軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, he was again made General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year 1 he was reappointed General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 二月，魯爽反叛，遣安都及冗從僕射胡子反、龍驤將軍宗越率步騎據歷陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lu Shuang rebelled; [the emperor] sent Andou, Supernumerary Attendant Hu Zifan, and General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry Zong Yue to lead infantry and cavalry and hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Shuang rebelled. The court sent Andou, Supernumerary Attendant Hu Zifan, and General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry Zong Yue with infantry and cavalry to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 爽遣將鄭德玄戍大峴，德玄使前鋒楊胡與輕兵向歷陽。

translations.literal: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian; Dexuan sent the vanguard Yang Hu with light troops toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan sent the vanguard Yang Hu with light troops against Liyang.

sentences.zh: 安都遣宗越及歷陽太守程天祚逆擊破之，斬胡與及其軍副。

translations.literal: Andou sent Zong Yue and the Administrator of Liyang Cheng Tianzuo to meet and defeat them, beheading Hu Yu and his deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Administrator Cheng Tianzuo to meet them, routed them, and beheaded Hu Yu and his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 德玄復使其司馬梁嚴屯峴東，安都幢主周文恭晨往偵候，因而襲之，悉禽；

translations.literal: Dexuan again sent his marshal Liang Yan to encamp east of Xian; Andou's banner chief Zhou Wengong went at dawn to reconnoiter and then raided them, capturing all;
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan sent his marshal Liang Yan to camp east of Xian. Andou's banner chief Zhou Wengong went out at dawn to scout, then attacked and took them all prisoner.

sentences.zh: 賊未敢進。

translations.literal: the rebels did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔安都留三百人守歷陽，渡還採石，遷輔國將軍、竟陵內史。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Andou to leave three hundred men to hold Liyang, cross back to Caishi, and be transferred to General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Andou to leave three hundred men at Liyang, cross back to Caishi, and promoted him to General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 四月，魯爽使弟瑜率三千人出小峴，爽尋以大眾阻大峴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Lu Shuang sent his younger brother Yu with three thousand men out through Little Xian; Shuang soon blocked Great Xian with his main force.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Lu Shuang sent his brother Yu with three thousand men through Little Xian while he himself blocked Great Xian with the main army.

sentences.zh: 又遣安都步騎八千度江，與歷陽太守張幼緒等討爽。

translations.literal: He again sent Andou with eight thousand infantry and cavalry across the river, together with the Administrator of Liyang Zhang Youxu and others, to campaign against Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Andou with eight thousand foot and horse across the Yangzi, together with Liyang Administrator Zhang Youxu and others, to crush Shuang.

sentences.zh: 安都軍副建武將軍譚金率數十騎挑戰，斬其偏帥。

translations.literal: Andou's deputy, General Who Establishes Martiality Tan Jin, led several dozen horsemen to challenge battle and beheaded a rebel flank commander.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's deputy, General Who Establishes Martiality Tan Jin, led several dozen horsemen into the fight and killed a rebel flank commander.

sentences.zh: 幼緒恇怯，輒引軍退還，安都復還歷陽。

translations.literal: Youxu was timid and cowardly and abruptly led his army back; Andou returned again to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu lost his nerve and pulled his troops back, so Andou withdrew to Liyang again.

sentences.zh: 臧質久不至，世祖復遣沈慶之濟江督統諸軍。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi was long in coming; the emperor again sent Shen Qingzhi across the river to take overall command of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi was slow to arrive, so the emperor sent Shen Qingzhi across the river to take command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 爽軍食少，引退，慶之使安都率輕騎追之；

translations.literal: Shuang's army had little food and withdrew; Qingzhi had Andou lead light cavalry in pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's army ran short of provisions and retreated. Qingzhi had Andou lead light cavalry in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 四月丙戌，及爽於小峴，爽自與腹心壯騎繼後。

translations.literal: on bingxu of the fourth month they caught Shuang at Little Xian; Shuang himself followed with his trusted stalwart horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day in the fourth month they caught Shuang at Little Xian. Shuang himself followed with his picked cavalry.

sentences.zh: 譚金先薄之，不能入，安都望見爽，便躍馬大呼，直往刺之，應手而倒，左右範雙斬爽首。

translations.literal: Tan Jin first pressed close but could not break in; Andou saw Shuang, spurred his horse, shouted loudly, charged straight to stab him—he fell at the blow—and his attendant Fan Shuang cut off Shuang's head.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jin closed first but could not break through. Andou saw Shuang, spurred forward with a shout, and ran him through at a single thrust. His attendant Fan Shuang took Shuang's head.

sentences.zh: 爽累世梟猛，生習戰陳，咸云萬人敵。

translations.literal: Shuang's family for generations had been fierce and bold; from birth he was practiced in battle arrays, and all said he was a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang came from a line famed for fierceness and had trained in battle from boyhood. Men called him a match for ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 安都單騎直入，斬之而反，時人皆云關羽之斬顏良，不是過也。

translations.literal: Andou alone on horseback charged straight in, killed him, and returned; people of the time all said that Guan Yu's slaying of Yan Liang was no greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Andou charged in alone, killed him, and rode back. Men of the day said it was no less than Guan Yu's killing of Yan Liang.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，增邑五百戶，并前千戶。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to marquis; his fief was increased by five hundred households, making one thousand together with the previous grant.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to marquis, with five hundred more households added to his fief for a total of one thousand.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨距南郡王義宣、臧質於梁山，安都復領騎為支軍。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xuanmo was holding off the Prince of Nanjun Yixuan and Zang Zhi at Liangshan; Andou again led cavalry as a supporting army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Xuanmo was holding Prince Yixuan of Nanjun and Zang Zhi at Liangshan. Andou again commanded the cavalry as a flanking force.

sentences.zh: 賊有水步營在蕪湖，安都遣將呂興壽率數十騎襲之，賊眾驚亂，斬首及赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels had water and land camps at Wuhu; Andou sent his general Lü Xingshou with several dozen horsemen to raid them—the rebel masses panicked and scattered, and very many were beheaded or drowned fleeing into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had river and land camps at Wuhu. Andou sent Lü Xingshou with several dozen horsemen to strike them. The enemy broke in panic, and a great many were killed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣將劉湛之及質攻玄謨，玄謨命眾軍擊之，使安都引騎出賊陣右。

translations.literal: Yixuan sent his generals Liu Chenzhi and Zhi to attack Xuanmo; Xuanmo ordered the armies to strike them and had Andou lead cavalry out to the right of the rebel formation.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent Liu Chenzhi and Zang Zhi against Xuanmo. Xuanmo ordered a general assault and sent Andou with the cavalry to the enemy's right flank.

sentences.zh: 譚金三歷賊陳，乘其隙縱騎突之，諸將係進。

translations.literal: Tan Jin thrice passed through the rebel lines; seizing an opening he loosed his horsemen in a charge, and the other generals pressed forward in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jin rode three times through the rebel lines, then charged through a gap with his cavalry while the other generals followed up.

sentences.zh: 是朝，賊馬軍發蕪湖，欲來會戰，望安都騎甚盛，隱山不敢出。

translations.literal: That morning the rebel horse army set out from Wuhu intending to join battle; seeing Andou's cavalry so strong, they hid in the hills and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: That morning rebel cavalry set out from Wuhu to join the fight, but seeing Andou's horsemen in such strength they hid in the hills and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 賊陣東南猶堅，安都橫擊陷之，賊遂大潰。

translations.literal: The rebel formation's southeast sector was still firm; Andou struck across and broke it, and the rebels then collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's southeast wing still held firm until Andou struck across and broke it. The rebels then fled in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 安都隊主劉元儒於艦中斬湛之首。

translations.literal: Andou's squad chief Liu Yuanru cut off Chen's head aboard a ship.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's squad chief Liu Yuanru cut off Chen's head on one of the ships.

sentences.zh: 轉太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，虜向無鹽，東平太守劉胡出戰失利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, the barbarians advanced on Wuyan; the Administrator of Dongping Liu Hu went out to fight and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 1 the Northern Wei advanced on Wuyan. Dongping Administrator Liu Hu met them in battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 二月，遣安都領馬軍北討，東陽太守沈法系水軍向彭城，並受徐州刺史申坦節度。

translations.literal: In the second month, [the court] sent Andou to lead the horse army on a northern campaign, and the Administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxing with the water army toward Pengcheng—all under the command of Xuzhou Inspector Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the court sent Andou north at the head of the cavalry and Dongyang Administrator Shen Faxing with the fleet toward Pengcheng, both under Xuzhou Inspector Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「賊若可及，便盡力殄之。

translations.literal: The emperor admonished them, saying: "If the enemy can be overtaken, exert yourselves to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned them: "If you can catch the enemy, destroy them with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 若度已回，可過河耀威而反。

translations.literal: If they have already turned back, you may cross the river to display might and return.
translations.idiomatic: If they have already withdrawn, cross the river to show your strength and come back.

sentences.zh: 」時虜已去，坦求回軍討任榛，見許。

translations.literal: " At that time the barbarians had already gone; Tan asked to turn the army back to campaign against Ren Zhen, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " By then the enemy had already left. Tan asked to turn the army against Ren Zhen, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 安都當向左城，左城去滑臺二百餘里，安都以去虜鎮近，軍少不宜分行。

translations.literal: Andou was to go toward Zuocheng; Zuocheng was more than two hundred li from Huatai. Andou judged that they were close to the barbarian garrisons and that with few troops they should not split forces.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was to march on Zuocheng, more than two hundred li from Huatai. He judged that they were too close to enemy garrisons and that with so few troops they should not divide their force.

sentences.zh: 至東坊城，遇任榛三騎，討擒其一，餘兩騎得走。

translations.literal: At Dongfangcheng they met three horsemen of Ren Zhen, captured one in pursuit, and the other two escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongfangcheng they met three of Ren Zhen's horsemen, captured one, and the other two got away.

sentences.zh: 任榛聞知，皆得逃散。

translations.literal: When Ren Zhen heard of this, all were able to flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Zhen heard of it, his men all scattered and escaped.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，水泉多竭，人馬疲困，不能遠追。

translations.literal: At that time there was drought; springs mostly dried up; men and horses were weary and could not pursue far.
translations.idiomatic: A drought had dried up most of the springs. Men and horses were exhausted and could not pursue far.

sentences.zh: 安都、法系並白衣領職，坦繫尚方。

translations.literal: Andou and Faxing both held their posts in plain dress [as punishment]; Tan was imprisoned in the Directorate of Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: Andou and Faxing were reduced to holding office in plain dress, and Tan was imprisoned in the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 任榛大抵在任城界，積世逋叛所聚，所在皆棘榛深密，難為用師，故能久自保藏，屢為民患。

translations.literal: Ren Zhen was mostly within the borders of Rencheng, a gathering place for long-term fugitive rebels; everywhere were dense thorn thickets, difficult for deploying troops, so they could long preserve themselves and repeatedly became a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhen operated chiefly in Rencheng, where generations of fugitive rebels had gathered. The country was thick with brambles and hard to campaign in, so they could hide for years and plague the people.

sentences.zh: 安都明年復職，改封武昌縣侯，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next year Andou was restored to office, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuchang, and given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Andou was restored to office, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuchang, and made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 七年，又加征虜將軍，為太子左衛率十年，終世祖世不轉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again given the additional rank General Who Conquers the Barbarians; he served ten years as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and was never transferred through the end of the Heir Apparent's reign.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was again made General Who Conquers the Barbarians. He held the post of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard for ten years and was never transferred for the rest of the emperor's reign.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月，索兒、光世竝在省，安都信催令速去，二人俱自省逃出，攜安都諸子及家累，席捲北奔。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, Suo'er and Guangshi were both at court; Andou's letter urged them to leave quickly. The two escaped together from the palace, took Andou's sons and household dependents, and swept north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taishi year 2, Suo'er and Guangshi were both at court. Andou's letter urged them to flee at once. The two escaped from the palace, took Andou's sons and families, and fled north in haste.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固並皆同反。

translations.literal: Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu and Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu both rebelled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu and Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu rebelled with him.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣劉彌之、張靈慶、崔僧琁三軍，道固遣子景征、傅靈越領眾，並應安都。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin; Daogu sent his son Jingzheng and Fu Lingyue to lead troops—all responding to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent the armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin. Daogu sent his son Jingzheng and Fu Lingyue with troops. All joined Andou.

sentences.zh: 彌之等南出下邳，靈越自泰山道向彭城。

translations.literal: Mizhi and the others marched south out of Xiapi; Lingyue took the Mount Tai route toward Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi and his force marched south from Xiapi while Lingyue advanced on Pengcheng by the Mount Tai road.

sentences.zh: 時濟陰太守申闡據睢陵城起義，索兒率靈越等攻之。

translations.literal: At that time the Administrator of Jiyin Shen Chan held Suiling city in revolt; Suo'er led Lingyue and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin Administrator Shen Chan had risen at Suiling. Suo'er led Lingyue and the rest against him.

sentences.zh: 安都使同黨裴祖隆守下邳城，彌之等至下邳，改計歸順，因進軍攻祖隆，僧琁不同，率所領歸安都。

translations.literal: Andou had his confederate Pei Zulong hold Xiapi; when Mizhi and the others reached Xiapi they changed plan and submitted, then advanced to attack Zulong. Sengqin did not agree and led his command back to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Andou had his ally Pei Zulong hold Xiapi. When Mizhi reached the city he changed sides and attacked Zulong. Sengqin refused and marched his men back to Andou.

sentences.zh: 索兒聞彌之有異志，舍睢陵馳赴下邳，彌之等未戰潰散，竝為索兒所執，見殺。

translations.literal: Suo'er heard Mizhi had changed allegiance, abandoned Suiling and galloped to Xiapi; Mizhi and the others collapsed without fighting, were all seized by Suo'er, and were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er heard that Mizhi had turned coat, abandoned Suiling, and raced to Xiapi. Mizhi's men broke without a fight, were seized by Suo'er, and executed.

sentences.zh: 時太宗以申令孫為徐州，代安都。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming made Shen Lingsun Inspector of Xuzhou to replace Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming then appointed Shen Lingsun Inspector of Xuzhou in Andou's place.

sentences.zh: 令孫進據淮陽，密有反志，遣人告索兒曰：「欲相從順，而百口在都。

translations.literal: Lingsun advanced and held Huaiyang, secretly harboring rebellious intent; he sent a man to tell Suo'er: "I wish to join you in submission, but my whole household is in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsun advanced and seized Huaiyang, secretly planning to rebel. He sent word to Suo'er: "I want to join you, but my whole family is in the capital.

sentences.zh: 可進軍見攻，若戰敗被執，家人可得免禍。

translations.literal: You may advance and appear to attack me; if I am defeated and captured, my family can be spared harm.
translations.idiomatic: March against me as if in earnest. If I am beaten and taken, my family may be spared.

sentences.zh: 」索兒乃遣靈越向淮陽，令孫出城，為相距之形，既而奔散，北投索兒。

translations.literal: " Suo'er then sent Lingyue toward Huaiyang; Lingsun came out of the city in the form of mutual opposition, then broke and fled north to join Suo'er.
translations.idiomatic: " Suo'er sent Lingyue against Huaiyang. Lingsun came out as if to fight, then broke and fled north to join Suo'er.

sentences.zh: 索兒使令孫說闡令降，闡既降，索兒執闡及令孫，並殺之。

translations.literal: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan had surrendered, Suo'er seized Chan and Lingsun and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender. When Chan yielded, Suo'er seized both Chan and Lingsun and killed them.

sentences.zh: 索兒因引軍渡淮，軍糧不給，掠奔百姓穀食。

translations.literal: Suo'er then led his army across the Huai; army provisions were insufficient, and they plundered grain from fleeing commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er then crossed the Huai. His army ran short of food and seized grain from fleeing civilians.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣齊王率前將軍張永、寧朔將軍垣山寶、王寬、員外散騎侍郎張寘震、蕭順之、龍驤將軍張季和、黃文玉等諸軍北討。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent the Prince of Qi leading the armies of Forward General Zhang Yong, General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and others on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent the Prince of Qi north at the head of Forward General Zhang Yong, General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Gentleman Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，軍次平原，索兒等率馬步五千，列陳距戰，擊大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year the army halted at Pingyuan; Suo'er and others led five thousand horse and foot, formed battle lines to resist, and were struck and utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: That May the army halted at Pingyuan. Suo'er led five thousand horse and foot into battle and was routed.

sentences.zh: 索兒又虜掠民穀，固守石樑，齊王又率鎮北參軍趙曇之、呂湛之擊之。

translations.literal: Suo'er again plundered the people's grain and held firm at Shiliang; the Prince of Qi again led the Northern Campaign staff officers Zhao Tanzhi and Lü Zhanzhi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er plundered grain again and held Shiliang. The Prince of Qi led his staff officers Zhao Tanzhi and Lü Zhanzhi against him.

sentences.zh: 索兒軍無資實，所資野掠，既見攻逼，無以自守，於是奔散；

translations.literal: Suo'er's army had no real supplies and relied on plunder in the countryside; once pressed by attack, they could not hold and so fled and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er's army had no real stores and lived by raiding the countryside. Once hard pressed, they could not hold and broke apart.

sentences.zh: 又追破之於葛家白鵠。

translations.literal: They were again pursued and defeated at Gejia Baihe.
translations.idiomatic: They were pursued and defeated again at Gejia Baihe.

sentences.zh: 索兒走向樂平縣界，為申令孫子孝叔所斬。

translations.literal: Suo'er fled toward the border of Leping county and was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's son Xiaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er fled toward Leping county and was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's son Xiaoshu.

sentences.zh: 安都子道智、大將范雙走向合肥，詣南汝陰太守裴季降。

translations.literal: Andou's sons Daozhi and the great general Fan Shuang fled toward Hefei and went to the Administrator of Southern Ruyin Pei Ji to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's sons Daozhi and the great general Fan Shuang fled to Hefei and surrendered to Southern Ruyin Administrator Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 時武衛將軍王廣之領軍隸劉勔，攻殷琰於壽陽。

translations.literal: At that time Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi led troops under Liu Xu and attacked Yin Yan at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi commanded troops under Liu Xu and besieged Yin Yan at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 傅靈越奔逃，為廣之軍人所生禽，厲聲曰：「我傅靈越也。

translations.literal: Fu Lingyue fled and was captured alive by Guangzhi's soldiers; he cried out in a loud voice: "I am Fu Lingyue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lingyue fled but was taken alive by Guangzhi's men. He shouted: "I am Fu Lingyue.

sentences.zh: 汝得賊何不即殺？

translations.literal: You have caught the rebel—why do you not kill me at once?
translations.idiomatic: You have your rebel—why not kill me now?

sentences.zh: 」生送詣勔，勔躬自慰勞，詰其叛逆。

translations.literal: " He was sent alive to Xu; Xu personally comforted and questioned him about his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He was sent alive to Xu, who questioned him personally about his revolt.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「九州唱義，豈獨在我。

translations.literal: He replied: "The nine provinces rose in righteous cause—how could that be mine alone?
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The whole realm rose in revolt. How can that be laid on me alone?

sentences.zh: 」勔又問：「四方阻逆，無戰不禽，主上皆加以曠蕩，即其才用。

translations.literal: " Xu asked again: "Rebels everywhere have been blocked and defeated; in every battle they are captured. The sovereign has been magnanimous and employed them according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu asked again: "Rebels everywhere have been beaten and taken. The emperor has been generous and used them according to their gifts.

sentences.zh: 卿何不早歸天闕，乃逃命草間乎？

translations.literal: Why did you not early return to the imperial court, but flee for your life among the weeds?
translations.idiomatic: Why did you not come back to court sooner instead of hiding in the grass?

sentences.zh: 」靈越答曰：「薛公舉兵淮北，威震天下，不能專任智勇，委付子侄，致敗之由，實在於此。

translations.literal: " Lingyue answered: "Lord Xue raised troops north of the Huai, his might shaking the realm, yet he could not entrust affairs solely to the wise and brave but delegated to sons and nephews—the real cause of defeat lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingyue answered: "Lord Xue raised the north of the Huai and shook the realm, yet he would not rely on the wise and brave alone but handed power to sons and nephews. That is why he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 然事之始末，備皆參豫，人生歸於一死，實無面求活。

translations.literal: Yet from beginning to end of the affair I took part in all of it; human life ends in death, and I truly have no face with which to beg to live.
translations.idiomatic: Still, I took part in it from start to finish. A man's life ends in death, and I have no face left to beg for my life.

sentences.zh: 」勔壯其意，送還京師。

translations.literal: " Xu admired his spirit and sent him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu admired his spirit and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲加原宥，靈越辭對如一，終不回改，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wished to pardon him, but Lingyue answered just as before and would not change; he was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wished to spare him, but Lingyue answered as before and would not yield. He was executed.

sentences.zh: 靈越，清河人也。

translations.literal: Lingyue was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 時輔國將軍、山陽內史程天祚據郡同安都，攻圍彌時，然後歸順。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo held his command together with Andou; after a long siege he then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo had held his command with Andou. After a long siege he submitted.

sentences.zh: 子勛平定，安都遣別駕從事史畢眾愛、下邳太守王煥等奉啟書詣太宗歸款，曰：「臣庸隸荒萌，偷生上國，過蒙世祖孝武皇帝過常之恩，犬馬有心，實感恩遇。

translations.literal: After Zixun was pacified, Andou sent his Registrar and Attendant Clerk Bi Zhong'ai, Administrator of Xiapi Wang Huan, and others to present a memorial to Emperor Ming offering submission, saying: "Your servant, a crude bondsman from the wild borderlands, stole life in the superior state and received beyond measure the exceptional grace of Emperor Xiaowu; this dog-and-horse heart truly feels gratitude for the favor shown.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun was crushed, Andou sent his registrar Bi Zhong'ai, Xiapi Administrator Wang Huan, and others to Emperor Ming with a letter of surrender: "I am a crude man from the frontier who has lived on your grace. Emperor Xiaowu favored me beyond merit, and this humble servant is truly grateful.

sentences.zh: 是以晉安始唱，投誠孤往，不期生榮，實存死報。

translations.literal: Therefore when Jin'an first raised the call, I went alone in loyal submission, not expecting glory in life but keeping faith to repay in death.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin'an first rose I went to him alone in good faith, not hoping for glory in life but ready to repay with death.

sentences.zh: 今天命大歸，群迷改屬，輒率領所部，束骸待誅，違拒之罪，伏聽湯鑊。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's mandate has returned in full, the deluded masses have changed allegiance, and I lead my command to bind my body and await execution; for the crime of resistance I bow to the boiling cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven's mandate has returned and the deluded have turned back. I lead my men to bind ourselves and await punishment. For resisting, I submit to whatever sentence you decree.

sentences.zh: 」索兒之死也，安都使柳光世守下邳，至是亦率所領歸降。

translations.literal: " When Suo'er died, Andou had Liu Guangshi hold Xiapi; by this time he too led his command in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " After Suo'er's death Andou had Liu Guangshi hold Xiapi. He too now surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 太宗以四方已平，欲示威於淮外，遣張永、沈攸之以重軍迎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, since the four quarters were already pacified, wished to display might beyond the Huai and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy army to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm pacified, Emperor Ming wished to show his might beyond the Huai and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a large army to receive him.

sentences.zh: 安都謂既已歸順，不應遣重兵，懼不免罪，乃遣信要引索虜。

translations.literal: Andou judged that having already submitted, a heavy army ought not to be sent; fearing he could not escape punishment, he sent a message inviting the Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Andou thought that having submitted he should not face a large army. Fearing punishment, he sent to invite the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，索虜遣博陵公尉遲苟人、城陽公孔伯恭二萬騎救之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the Northern Wei sent the Duke of Boling Yuchi Gouren and the Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong with twenty thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3 the Northern Wei sent Duke Yuchi Gouren of Boling and Duke Kong Bogong of Chengyang with twenty thousand horsemen to his aid.

sentences.zh: 永等引退，安都開門納虜，虜即授安都徐州刺史、河東公。

translations.literal: Yong and the others withdrew; Andou opened the gates and admitted the barbarians, who at once appointed him Inspector of Xuzhou and Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and the others withdrew. Andou opened the gates to the enemy, who made him Inspector of Xuzhou and Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，召還桑乾。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he was summoned back to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 4 he was summoned back to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 五年，死於虜中，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died among the barbarians, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he died in the north, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 初，安都起兵，長史蘭陵儼密欲圖之，見殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Andou raised troops, his Chief Clerk Lanling Yan secretly plotted against him and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou first rebelled, his chief clerk Lanling Yan secretly plotted against him and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 安都未向桑乾，前軍將軍裴祖隆謀殺苟人，舉彭城歸順，事泄，見誅。

translations.literal: Before Andou went to Sanggan, Forward General Pei Zulong plotted to kill Gouren and raise Pengcheng in submission; the affair leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before Andou went to Sanggan, Forward General Pei Zulong plotted to kill Gouren and surrender Pengcheng. The plot was discovered and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎孫耿之擊索兒戰死，及劉彌之、張靈慶皆戰敗見殺，並為太宗所哀，追贈儼光祿勳，祖隆寧朔將軍、兗州刺史，耿之羽林監，彌之輔國將軍、青州刺史，靈慶寧朔將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Sun Gengzhi died fighting Suo'er; Liu Mizhi and Zhang Lingqing were also defeated in battle and killed—all were mourned by Emperor Ming, who posthumously enfeoffed Yan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Zulong as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou, Gengzhi as Colonel of the Forest of Feathers, Mizhi as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qingzhou, and Lingqing as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Gentleman Sun Gengzhi died fighting Suo'er. Liu Mizhi and Zhang Lingqing were also killed in battle. Emperor Ming mourned them all and posthumously honored Yan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Zulong as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou, Gengzhi as Colonel of the Forest of Feathers, Mizhi as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qingzhou, and Lingqing as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 安都子伯令、環龍，亡命梁、雍二州之間。

translations.literal: Andou's sons Boling and Huanlong were outlaws between the Liang and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's sons Boling and Huanlong became outlaws between Liang and Yong.

sentences.zh: 三年，率亡命數千人襲廣平，執太守劉冥虯，攻順陽，克之，略有義成、扶風，置立守宰。

translations.literal: In the third year they led several thousand outlaws to raid Guangping, seized Administrator Liu Mingqiu, attacked Shunyang and took it, and briefly held Yicheng and Fufeng, setting up local officials.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 they led several thousand outlaws against Guangping, seized Administrator Liu Mingqiu, took Shunyang, and briefly held Yicheng and Fufeng, appointing local officials.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史巴陵王休若遣南陽太守張敬兒、新野太守劉攘兵擊破之，並禽。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector the Prince of Baling Xiuruo sent the Administrators of Nanyang Zhang Jing'er and Xinye Liu Rangbing to defeat them and capture them both.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Inspector Prince Xiuruo of Baling sent Nanyang Administrator Zhang Jing'er and Xinye Administrator Liu Rangbing against them. Both brothers were defeated and captured.

sentences.zh: 先是，東安、東莞二郡太守張讜守團城，在彭城東北。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Administrator of Dong'an and Dongguan Zhang Chan held Tuancheng, northeast of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dong'an and Dongguan Administrator Zhang Chan had held Tuancheng, northeast of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 始同安都，末亦歸順，太宗以為東徐州刺史，復為虜所沒。

translations.literal: At first he joined Andou, but in the end also submitted; Emperor Ming made him Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, but the territory was again lost to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He had first joined Andou but later submitted. Emperor Ming made him Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, but the region was lost again to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，遷督青州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、建威將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was transferred to supervise all military affairs of Dongguan and Dong'an in Qingzhou, as General Who Establishes Martiality and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 1 he was made supervisor of military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an in Qingzhou, General Who Establishes Martiality, and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時帝狂悖無道，內外憂危，文秀將之鎮，部曲出屯白下，說慶之曰：「主上狂暴如此，土崩將至，而一門受其寵任，萬物皆謂與之同心。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was mad and lawless; within and without all were anxious and imperiled. As Wenxiu was about to go to his post, his troops encamped at Baixia, and he said to Qingzhi: "The sovereign is so violent and cruel that collapse is near, yet our whole house enjoys his favor and all think us of one mind with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was mad and cruel, and the court was in peril. As Wenxiu set out for his post his troops camped at Baixia. He told Qingzhi: "The sovereign is so violent that the realm will soon fall apart, yet our whole house enjoys his favor and everyone thinks us loyal to him.

sentences.zh: 且此人性情無常，猜忌特甚，將來之禍，事又難測。

translations.literal: Moreover this man's temperament is fickle and his suspicion extreme; the calamity to come is hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: His temper is fickle and his suspicion extreme. The disaster ahead is impossible to foresee.

sentences.zh: 今因此眾力，圖之易於反掌，千載一時，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Now with this force at hand, to plot against him would be easier than turning the hand—an opportunity of a thousand years, not to be lost.
translations.idiomatic: With this force at hand we could overthrow him as easily as turning the hand. Such a chance comes once in a thousand years and must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 」慶之不從。

translations.literal: " Qingzhi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 文秀固請非一，言輒流涕，終不回。

translations.literal: Wenxiu pressed him again and again, weeping as he spoke, but in the end [Qingzhi] would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu pleaded again and again, weeping as he spoke, but Qingzhi would not change his mind.

sentences.zh: 文秀既行，慶之果為帝所殺。

translations.literal: After Wenxiu had departed, Qingzhi was indeed killed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxiu left, Qingzhi was indeed killed by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 慶之死後，帝遣直閣江方興領兵誅文秀，方興未至，太宗已定亂，馳驛駐之。

translations.literal: After Qingzhi's death the emperor sent the Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing with troops to execute Wenxiu; Fangxing had not yet arrived when Emperor Ming had already settled the turmoil and sent a post horse to halt him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qingzhi's death the emperor sent Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing to kill Wenxiu. Before Fangxing arrived, Emperor Ming had already put down the revolt and sent orders to stop him.

sentences.zh: 方興既至，為文秀所執。

translations.literal: When Fangxing arrived he was seized by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangxing arrived, Wenxiu seized him.

sentences.zh: 尋見釋，遣還京師。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon released and sent back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時晉安王子勛據尋陽反叛，六師外討，徵兵於文秀。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Jin'an Zixun held Xunyang in rebellion; the six armies campaigned abroad and levied troops from Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zixun of Jin'an held Xunyang in rebellion. The six armies marched out and called on Wenxiu for troops.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣劉彌之、張靈慶、崔僧琁三軍赴朝廷。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin to join the court forces.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent the armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin to the court.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都已同子勛，遣使報文秀，以四方齊舉，勸令同逆，文秀即令彌之等回應安都。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had already joined Zixun; he sent a messenger to inform Wenxiu that all quarters were rising together and urged him to rebel likewise; Wenxiu at once ordered Mizhi and the others to respond to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had already joined Zixun. He sent word that the whole realm was rising and urged Wenxiu to rebel too. Wenxiu ordered Mizhi and the rest to join Andou.

sentences.zh: 彌之等尋歸順，事在安都傳。

translations.literal: Mizhi and the others soon submitted—the account is in Andou's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi and the others soon submitted—the account is in Andou's biography.

sentences.zh: 彌之青州強姓，門族甚多，諸宗從相合率奔北海，據城以拒文秀。

translations.literal: Mizhi was of a powerful Qingzhou clan with many kinsmen; the various collateral branches together fled to Beihai and held the city to resist Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi came from a powerful Qingzhou clan with many kinsmen. His relatives fled to Beihai together and held the city against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 平原、樂安二郡太守王玄默據琅邪，清河、廣川二郡太守王玄邈據盤陽城，高陽、勃海二郡太守劉乘民據臨濟城，並起義。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Pingyuan and Le'an Wang Xuanmo held Langye; the Administrators of Qinghe and Guangchuan Wang Xuanyao held Panyang city; the Administrators of Gaoyang and Bohai Liu Chengmin held Linji city—all rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan and Le'an Administrator Wang Xuanmo held Langye; Qinghe and Guangchuan Administrator Wang Xuanyao held Panyang; Gaoyang and Bohai Administrator Liu Chengmin held Linji—all rose against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 文秀司馬房文慶謀應之，為文秀所殺。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's marshal Fang Wenqing plotted to join them and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu's marshal Fang Wenqing plotted to join them and was executed by Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣軍主解彥士攻北海陷之，乘民從弟伯宗合率鄉兵，復克北海，因率所領向青州所治東陽城。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent the army commander Xie Yanshi to attack Beihai and take it; Chengmin's cousin Bozong gathered local militia, retook Beihai, and then led his command toward Dongyang city, seat of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent army commander Xie Yanshi against Beihai and took it. Chengmin's cousin Bozong rallied local militia, retook Beihai, and marched on Dongyang, the Qingzhou capital.

sentences.zh: 文秀拒之，伯宗戰敗被創，弟天愛扶持將去，伯宗曰：「丈夫當死戰場，以身殉國，安能歸死兒女手中乎！

translations.literal: Wenxiu resisted him; Bozong was defeated in battle and wounded. His younger brother Tian'ai supported him to leave, but Bozong said: "A man should die on the battlefield, giving his body for the state—how can he go home to die in the hands of women and children!
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu resisted him. Bozong was beaten and wounded. His brother Tian'ai tried to carry him away, but Bozong said: "A man should die on the battlefield for his country. How can I go home to die like a child in women's hands?

sentences.zh: 弟可速去，無為兩亡。

translations.literal: Brother, go quickly—do not let us both perish.
translations.idiomatic: Brother, go at once. Do not let us both die.

sentences.zh: 」乃見殺，追贈龍驤將軍、長廣太守。

translations.literal: " He was then killed; posthumously he was given the rank General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then killed. He was posthumously made General Who Leads the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣青州刺史明僧皓、東莞、東安二郡太守李靈謙率軍伐文秀。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Senghao and the Administrator of Dongguan and Dong'an Li Lingqian with armies to campaign against Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Senghao and Dongguan and Dong'an Administrator Li Lingqian against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 玄邈、乘民、僧皓等並進軍攻城，每戰輒為文秀所破，離而復合，如此者十餘。

translations.literal: Xuanyao, Chengmin, Senghao, and the others all advanced to besiege the city; in every battle they were broken by Wenxiu, withdrew, and joined again—more than ten times in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyao, Chengmin, Senghao, and the others besieged the city. Wenxiu beat them in every fight. They withdrew and returned more than ten times.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月，尋陽平定，太宗遣尚書度支郎崔元孫慰勞諸義軍，隨僧皓戰敗見殺，追贈寧朔將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, Xunyang was pacified; Emperor Ming sent the Secretary of the Board of Revenue Cui Yuansun to comfort the righteous armies; he followed Senghao, was defeated in battle and killed, and was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Taishi year 2 Xunyang fell. Emperor Ming sent Secretary Cui Yuansun to reward the loyal armies. He followed Senghao, was defeated and killed, and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣文秀弟文炳詔文秀曰：「皇帝前問督青州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、建威將軍、青州刺史，朕去歲撥亂，功振普天，於卿一門，特有殊澤，卿得延命至今，誰之力邪？

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing with an edict to Wenxiu, saying: "The emperor inquires of the supervisor of military affairs in Qingzhou and in Dongguan and Dong'an of Xuzhou, General Who Establishes Martiality and Inspector of Qingzhou: Last year I put down disorder and my merit shook the whole realm; to your house alone I showed special grace—you have prolonged your life until now; whose power is that?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wenxiu's brother Wenbing with an edict: "The emperor asks the supervisor of Qingzhou and of Dongguan and Dong'an in Xuzhou, General Who Establishes Martiality and Inspector of Qingzhou: Last year I restored order and my merit shook the realm. Your house alone I favored. You have lived until now—whose doing is that?

sentences.zh: 何故背國負恩，遠同逆豎。

translations.literal: Why then betray the state and repay kindness with ingratitude, joining the rebel villains far away?
translations.idiomatic: Why then betray the state and join rebels far away?

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，四方寧一，卿獨守窮城，何所歸奉？

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled and the four quarters at peace—why do you alone hold this desperate city; to whom will you turn?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is settled and the four quarters at peace. Why do you alone hold this doomed city? To whom will you turn?

sentences.zh: 且卿百口在都，兼有墳墓，想情非木石，猶或顧懷。

translations.literal: Moreover your whole household is in the capital, and you have ancestral graves besides; I trust your feelings are not stone and wood, and you may yet look back with care.
translations.idiomatic: Your whole family is in the capital, and you have ancestral graves there. You are not made of wood and stone—you must still care for them.

sentences.zh: 故指遣文炳具相宣示。

translations.literal: Therefore I send Wenbing to set this forth in full.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I send Wenbing to tell you all this.

sentences.zh: 凡諸逆郎，親為戎首，一不加罪，文炳所具。

translations.literal: As for all the rebel leaders who personally led the armies, not one was punished—Wenbing will explain this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: All the rebel leaders who led the armies in person have been spared punishment, as Wenbing will explain.

sentences.zh: 卿獨何人，而能自立。

translations.literal: Who are you alone, that you can stand apart?
translations.idiomatic: Who are you to stand apart alone?

sentences.zh: 便可速率部曲，同到軍門，別詔有司，一無所問。

translations.literal: You may at once lead your command swiftly to the army gate; a separate edict to the officials will question you on nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Come at once with your troops to the army gate. A separate edict will spare you from all inquiry.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，國有常刑，非惟戮及弟息，亦當夷卿墳壟，既以謝齊土百姓，亦以勞將士之心。

translations.literal: If you do not, the state has its fixed punishments—not only will your sons and younger brothers be executed, but your ancestral graves will also be leveled, both to answer the people of Qi and to satisfy the hearts of the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, the state has its fixed punishments. Not only your sons and brothers will die—your ancestral graves will be destroyed as well, both to answer the people of Qi and to satisfy the army.

sentences.zh: 故有今詔。

translations.literal: Hence this present edict.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this edict.

sentences.zh: 」三年二月，文秀歸命請罪，即安本任。

translations.literal: " In the second month of the third year, Wenxiu submitted and begged pardon, and was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month of year 3 Wenxiu submitted and begged pardon, and was restored to his original post.

sentences.zh: 先是，冀州刺史崔道固亦據歷城同逆，為土人起義所攻，與文秀俱遣信引虜；

translations.literal: Earlier, Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu had also held Licheng in rebellion together with Wenxiu; he was attacked by local uprisings and, together with Wenxiu, sent messages inviting the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu had also held Licheng in rebellion. Local uprisings attacked him, and he and Wenxiu both invited the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 虜遣將慕輿白曜率大眾援之，文秀已受朝命，乃乘虜無備，縱兵掩擊，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: the barbarians sent the general Murong Baiyao with a great host to aid them; Wenxiu had already received the court's commission and, taking advantage of the enemy's lack of preparation, loosed his troops in a surprise attack and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent General Murong Baiyao with a large force to aid them. Wenxiu had already received the court's commission and, catching the enemy unprepared, struck by surprise and killed or wounded many.

sentences.zh: 虜乃進軍圍城，文秀善於撫御，將士咸為盡力，每與虜戰，輒摧破之，掩擊營寨，往無不捷。

translations.literal: The barbarians then advanced to besiege the city; Wenxiu was skilled at winning men over, and officers and soldiers all strove for him with their utmost; in every battle with the barbarians he broke them, and in raids on their camps he never failed to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then besieged the city. Wenxiu was skilled at winning men's hearts, and his officers and soldiers fought with all their strength. In every battle he broke the enemy, and in raids on their camps he never failed.

sentences.zh: 太宗進文秀號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming advanced Wenxiu's title to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming promoted Wenxiu to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，虜蜀郡公拔式等馬步數萬人入西郭，直至城下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year the barbarian Duke of Shujun Bashi and others with several tens of thousands of horse and foot entered the western suburb and reached the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: That August Duke Bashi of Shujun and others led tens of thousands of horse and foot into the western suburb and up to the walls.

sentences.zh: 文秀使輔國將軍垣諶擊破之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent General Who Assists the State Yuan Chen to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent General Who Assists the State Yuan Chen and routed them.

sentences.zh: 九月，又逼城東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they pressed the eastern wall again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they pressed the eastern wall again.

sentences.zh: 十月，進攻南郭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they advanced against the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they attacked the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 文秀使員外散騎侍郎黃彌之等邀擊，斬獲數千。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent Supernumerary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Huang Mizhi and others to intercept them, beheading and capturing several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent Supernumerary Gentleman Huang Mizhi and others to intercept them and killed or captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 四年，又進文秀號右將軍，封新城縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wenxiu's title was again advanced to General of the Right Army; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xincheng with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Wenxiu was promoted to General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xincheng with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 虜青州刺史王隆顯於安丘縣又為軍主高崇仁所破，死者數百人。

translations.literal: The barbarian Inspector of Qingzhou Wang Longxian was again defeated at Anqiu county by the army commander Gao Chongren; several hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy Qingzhou Inspector Wang Longxian was defeated again at Anqiu by army commander Gao Chongren, with several hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 虜圍青州積久，太宗所遣救兵並不敢進，乃以文秀弟征北中兵參軍文靜為輔國將軍，統高密、北海、平昌、長廣、東萊五郡軍事，從海道救青州。

translations.literal: The barbarians had long besieged Qingzhou; the relief armies the court sent did not dare advance, so Wenxiu's younger brother the acting staff officer of the Northern Campaign Central Army Wen Jing was made General Who Assists the State, commanding military affairs of the five commanderies Gaomi, Beihai, Pingchang, Changguang, and Donglai, to rescue Qingzhou by sea.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had long besieged Qingzhou, and the relief armies the court sent would not advance. Wenxiu's brother Wen Jing, acting staff officer of the northern campaign, was made General Who Assists the State to command five commanderies and relieve Qingzhou by sea.

sentences.zh: 文靜至東萊之不其城，為虜所斷遏，不得進，因保城自守，又為虜所攻，屢戰輒克，太宗加其東青州刺史。

translations.literal: Wen Jing reached Buqi city in Donglai but was blocked by the barbarians and could not advance; he therefore held the city in defense, was again attacked by the barbarians, and in repeated battles always prevailed; Emperor Ming added the title Inspector of Eastern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jing reached Buqi in Donglai but was blocked by the enemy and could not advance. He held the city and beat off repeated attacks. Emperor Ming made him Inspector of Eastern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，不其城為虜所陷，文靜見殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Buqi fell to the barbarians and Wen Jing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Buqi fell to the enemy and Wen Jing was killed.

sentences.zh: 文秀被圍三載，外無援軍，士卒為之用命，無離叛者，日夜戰鬥，甲胄生蟣虱。

translations.literal: Wenxiu was besieged for three years; there was no relief army from without, yet the soldiers gave him their lives and none deserted; day and night they fought, and lice bred in their armor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu was besieged for three years with no relief from outside, yet his men fought to the death and none deserted. They fought day and night until lice bred in their armor.

sentences.zh: 五年正月二十四日，遂為虜所陷。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month of the fifth year the city at last fell to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month of year 5 the city fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 城敗之日，解釋戎衣，緩服靜坐，命左右取所持節。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell he removed his military dress, sat calmly in plain robes, and ordered his attendants to bring the staff of office he carried.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the city fell he took off his armor, sat calmly in plain robes, and ordered his attendants to bring his staff of office.

sentences.zh: 虜既入，兵刃交至，問曰：「青州刺史沈文秀何在？

translations.literal: Once the barbarians had entered, weapons clashed all around; they asked: "Where is Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu?
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy entered, weapons clashed all around. They asked: "Where is Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu?

sentences.zh: 」文秀厲聲曰：「身是。

translations.literal: " Wenxiu cried in a loud voice: "I am he.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenxiu shouted: "I am he.

sentences.zh: 」因執之，牽出聽事前，剝取衣服。

translations.literal: " He was seized and dragged out before the hall of audience, where his clothes were stripped off.
translations.idiomatic: " He was seized and dragged before the hall, where his clothes were stripped off.

sentences.zh: 時白曜在城西南角樓，裸縛文秀至曜前，執之者令拜。

translations.literal: At that time Baiyao was on the tower at the southwest corner of the city; Wenxiu was bound naked and brought before Baiyao, and those holding him ordered him to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was on the tower at the southwest corner. Wenxiu was bound naked and brought before him. His captors ordered him to bow.

sentences.zh: 文秀曰：「各二國大臣，無相拜之禮。

translations.literal: " Wenxiu said: "We are ministers of two states—there is no ritual of bowing to one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenxiu said: "We are ministers of two states. There is no bowing between us.

sentences.zh: 」曜命還其衣，為設酒食，鏁送桑乾。

translations.literal: " Baiyao ordered his clothes returned, had food and wine set out, and sent him in chains to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao had his clothes returned, gave him food and wine, and sent him in chains to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 其餘為亂兵所殺，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The rest were killed by the disorderly troops; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were killed by the disorderly troops. The dead were very many.

sentences.zh: 太宗先遣尚書功論郎何如真選青州文武，亦為虜所殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had earlier sent the Secretary for Merit Evaluation He Ruzhen to select Qingzhou civil and military men; he too was killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had earlier sent Secretary He Ruzhen to select Qingzhou officials. He too was killed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 文秀在桑乾凡十九年，齊之永明四年，病死，時年六十一。

translations.literal: Wenxiu was at Sanggan altogether nineteen years; in the fourth year of Yongming of Qi he died of illness, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu spent nineteen years at Sanggan. In Yongming year 4 of Qi he died of illness, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 崔道固，清河人也。

translations.literal: Cui Daogu was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，以幹用見知，歷太子屯騎校尉，左軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Heir Apparent's reign he was known for capability and served as Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Escort Cavalry and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the emperor he was known for ability and served as Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Escort Cavalry and General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，出為齊、北海二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he went out as Administrator of Qi and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 3 he was made Administrator of Qi and Beihai.

sentences.zh: 民焦恭破古塚，得玉鎧，道固檢得，獻之，執繫恭。

translations.literal: A commoner named Jiao Gong broke open an ancient tomb and obtained a jade suit of armor; Daogu seized it on inspection, presented it [to the throne], and had Gong arrested.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Jiao Gong opened an ancient tomb and found a jade suit of armor. Daogu seized it, presented it to the throne, and had Gong arrested.

sentences.zh: 入為新安王子鸞北中郎諮議參軍，永嘉王子仁左軍司馬。

translations.literal: He entered court as Consultative Staff Officer to the Northern Central Commander for the Prince of Xin'an Ziluan and as Marshal of the Left Army for the Prince of Yongjia Ziren.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as staff officer to Northern Central Commander Prince Ziluan of Xin'an and as marshal of the left army to Prince Ziren of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，出為寧朔將軍、冀州刺史，鎮歷城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou, stationed at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 1 he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou, with his seat at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，進號輔國將軍，又進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi his title was advanced to General Who Assists the State, and again to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 2 he was promoted to General Who Assists the State and then to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都同逆，上即還道固本號為徐州代之。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had joined the rebellion; the emperor at once restored Daogu's original title and had him replace Andou as Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had rebelled. The emperor at once restored Daogu's former rank and made him Inspector of Xuzhou in Andou's place.

sentences.zh: 道固不受命，遣子景微、軍主傅靈越率眾赴安都。

translations.literal: Daogu would not accept the commission and sent his son Jingwei and the army commander Fu Lingyue with troops to join Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu refused the appointment and sent his son Jingwei and army commander Fu Lingyue with troops to join Andou.

sentences.zh: 既而為土人起義所攻，屢戰失利，閉門自守。

translations.literal: Soon he was attacked by local uprisings, suffered repeated defeats in battle, and shut the gates to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon attacked by local rebels, lost battle after battle, and shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 會四方平定，上遣使宣慰，道固奉詔歸順。

translations.literal: When the four quarters were pacified, the emperor sent envoys to proclaim comfort; Daogu received the edict and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was pacified, the emperor sent envoys to reassure him. Daogu accepted the edict and submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是與沈文秀共引虜，虜既至，固守距之，因被圍逼。

translations.literal: Earlier he and Shen Wenxiu had together invited the barbarians; once the barbarians arrived he held firm to resist them and was therefore besieged and pressed.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shen Wenxiu had earlier invited the Northern Wei together. When the enemy arrived he held the city against them and was besieged.

sentences.zh: 虜每進，輒為道固所摧。

translations.literal: Whenever the barbarians advanced, they were broken by Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the enemy advanced, Daogu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 三年，以為都督冀、青、兗、幽、并五州諸軍事、前將軍、冀州刺史，加節，又進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made commander of all military affairs in the five provinces Jizhou, Qingzhou, Yanzhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou, as Forward General and Inspector of Jizhou, with staff of authority, and his title was again advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made commander of military affairs in Jizhou, Qingzhou, Yanzhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou, Forward General and Inspector of Jizhou with staff of authority, and promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 其年，為虜所陷，被送桑乾，死於虜中。

translations.literal: That year the city fell to the barbarians; he was sent to Sanggan and died among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: That year the city fell. He was sent to Sanggan and died in the north.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《春秋》列國大夫得罪，皆先致其邑而後去，唯邾、莒三臣，書以叛人之目，蓋重地也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when great officers of the feudal states offended, they all first surrendered their fiefs and then departed; only the three ministers of Zhu and Ju are recorded under the heading of rebels—because territory weighs heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when feudal ministers offended their lords they surrendered their fiefs before leaving. Only the three ministers of Zhu and Ju are called rebels in the text—because land is what matters most.

sentences.zh: 安都勤王之略，義闕於藩屏，以地外奔，罪同於三叛。

translations.literal: Andou's plan to aid the sovereign lacked righteousness in his role as a screen of the realm; fleeing abroad with his territory, his crime was the same as the three rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's plan to aid the throne failed the duty of a frontier shield. He fled north with his territory, and his crime was the same as those three rebels.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「誰生厲階，至今為梗。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Who raised this mischief—down to today it remains a stumbling block.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Who raised this trouble? Down to today it remains a stumbling block.

sentences.zh: 」其此之謂乎？

translations.literal: " Is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: " Is this not what is meant?
